tutorial.d1: Your first day in the House. You know nobody yet. Bills get their first reading today; nothing comes to a vote. Tonight the whip's office may want a word. Tap MPs to see what you know about them (not much), and open the Book for everyone.
tutorial.d2: Votes come up most sitting days. Routine ones settle on their own; the game stops you for votes that matter to you. Watch your mentor tonight: they know people.
tutorial.d3: Wednesday: caucus. The party meets behind closed doors before the House sits. Listen to read the room, speak once, whisper to a neighbour.
tutorial.d4: Thursday. The vote your riding has been waiting for is on the order paper.
tutorial.d5: Friday: the riding. The whip lets rookies go home in their first week. The people who elected you are waiting.

aim.label: Your aim
aim.title: Act {n} · {rank}
aim.1: Get the whip's office to notice you.
aim.2: Make your name, then win the next seat in the whip's office.
aim.3: Deliver your row: about fifteen members, some of them your friends.
aim.4: Run the count without getting it wrong, and build the support to be Chief Whip.
aim.5: Hold the caucus and keep the government standing.
aim.how.1: Every vote on the record counts. A loyal vote counts a little; a rebellion counts more, and goes in the whip's file. A question in Question Period, a word in caucus and a committee seat count too. Reliable or useful trouble: either way gets you to Act 2, with a different reputation.
aim.how.2: When a seat opens in the whip's office, the whip picks you or your rival. What counts: the whip's opinion of you, your mentor, your clique, and how often you've been noticed. Rebellions count against you now.
aim.how.3: A vote is carried when someone in your row was wavering and nobody broke. If three of your row break on a close or confidence vote, you're back on the backbench.
aim.how.4: Call a government vote safe and lose it, and you're back to assistant whip. When the Chief Whip's chair opens, you need the caucus or the leader behind you.
aim.how.5: Each Monday you set the line with the leader. If caucus support falls below {floor}, the room can turn on you. If the pressure on the office reaches {top}, the leader replaces you. You can retire whenever you choose.
aim.wait.2: You've served long enough. A seat in the whip's office can open any weekend now.
aim.wait.4: You've served long enough. The Chief Whip's chair can open any weekend now.
aim.fell: You've been here before. The whip's office remembers you, and that cuts both ways: half of what got you noticed still counts, and the rest you earn again.
job.label: Your job here
job.morning: Read what's coming up. Most votes settle themselves; you'll be called in for the ones that need you.
job.morning.ownVote: A vote marked “Your vote” is today. When the bells ring you'll pick a side, so know which before you go in.
job.morning.whip: Check today's whipped votes against the count. If one looks short, the bells are your last chance to fix it.
job.morning.bigVote: Today is the week's vote. The talking is done: what's left is the bells and your own vote.
job.morning.none: No votes today. The work is in the office tonight.
job.office: You have {n} blocks of time tonight. Spend them on people: every meeting teaches you something, and some end in a deal.
job.office.called: Go to the whip's office first: ignoring the whip costs you. Then spend the rest of your {n} blocks on people.
job.office.whip: Tomorrow's count is on the board. Spend your {n} blocks on the members who are wavering, not the ones already with you.
job.office.fell: Back on the backbench. They remember you; that cuts both ways. Spend your {n} blocks winning back the people who stopped returning your calls.
job.meeting.whipCall: The whip wants you to vote {pos}. Get something for it, or turn the whip down and live with it.
job.meeting.rebelRecruit: They want you to break with the line. Hear them out; agreeing is up to you.
job.meeting.favorAsk: They want a favour. Grant it and they owe you; refuse and they'll remember.
job.meeting.introduction: A first proper meeting. Listen well and you'll learn what they want.
job.meeting.gossip: They have news from the lobby. Listen, and you'll learn something about someone.
job.meeting.complaint: They're unhappy with you. Patch it up, or decide they're not worth the time.
job.meeting.mentorAdvice: Your mentor knows who matters. Listen.
job.meeting.other: Read them first, then see what they'll trade.
job.caucus: Read the room. You have three moves: listen to learn the mood, speak once to take a side, whisper to work on a neighbour.
job.caucus.chief: Your caucus now. Keep enough of the room with you: below {floor} support, they can come for you. You can free a whipped vote, or put a member out.
job.caucus.revolt: A revolt against the leader is on the table. Back the leader, join it, or keep your head down. The room sees which.
job.caucus.revoltYou: The revolt is against you. Face them down or let the room decide; everyone you leaned on to get here is watching.
job.qp: Ask your question. Keeping to the line pleases the whip; pressing the minister gets you noticed if it lands; naming the thing at home plays in the riding.
job.division.dilemma: Pick a lobby. The line is {pos}; your riding or your conscience pulls the other way. Everyone sees which you choose.
job.division.line: The line is {pos}. Vote it, break it, or be somewhere else.
job.division.free: A free vote. Nobody is whipping this one: vote as you see fit.
job.division.confidence: The line is {pos}, and nobody forgets who broke it on a night like this.
job.division.chase: Get your missing members into the chamber before the doors close, then cast your own vote. The line is {pos}.
job.division.ownBill: Your bill. The votes you lined up in the office have to turn up now.
job.division.bigVote: The week's vote. The line is {pos}, and everything you did since Monday is about to be read out, name by name.
job.riding: Hear your constituents. Standing here decides your nomination and your seat. A case you carry stays yours until it comes up in Question Period.
job.campaign: The House is dissolved. Spend the campaign where it helps most: standing at home decides your seat.
